title: Ownership & Moves
objectives: Predict which values move, copy, or stay
body:
# Ownership & Moves

## The three rules

1. Every value has exactly one **owner**.
2. When the owner goes out of scope, the value is **dropped**.
3. Assignment / argument passing **moves** ownership (for non-`Copy` types).

## Move vs Copy vs Clone

```rust
let a = String::from("heap");
let b = a;              // MOVE: a is now invalid
// println!("{a}");     // ❌ E0382 borrow of moved value

let x = 5;
let y = x;              // COPY: i32 is Copy, both usable

let s = b.clone();      // explicit deep copy, both usable
```

`Copy` types: integers, floats, bool, char, shared refs. Anything owning heap
memory (`String`, `Vec`) moves instead — no double-free by construction.

## Functions take ownership too

```rust
fn consume(s: String) { println!("{s}"); } // s dropped here
fn give_back(mut s: String) -> String { s.push('!'); s }
```

Returning the value transfers ownership back out. This dance is exactly what
**borrowing** (next lesson) removes the need for.

## Drop timing = deterministic

Rust inserts `drop(value)` at end of scope. RAII: files close, locks release,
memory frees — without a garbage collector and without leaks-by-forgetting.
